beats.say: Updates are not just new buttons. Most of them close security holes that attackers already know about.
As soon as a hole is announced, attackers start hunting for devices that are not updated. Every day of delay adds risk.
A pop-up saying your browser is outdated, download now, is a trap. Browsers update from their own settings.
Real updates come from the device settings or the official app store. When in doubt, go there yourself and check.
Do not put off the restart after an update. Often the protection only takes effect once the device restarts.

messages.text: Virus detected on your phone! Download the security update: fix-phone.example.info/app.apk

cards.explain: Your phone does not send updates by SMS. This link installs a malicious app.

body.text: After 19:00 today, work computers will update automatically.
Leave your computer on and just save your work. You do not need to download anything.

cards.explain: No link, no file, nothing to download. It only informs you.
A site that says update your player to watch a video is a classic trap. Browsers play video on their own.

subject.text: Your licence is expiring! Update required

cards.explain: Updates do not arrive as email attachments. The archive may hide malware.

body.text: To update your computer remotely, install this program and send me the code on your screen.

cards.explain: A remote-control program gives the attacker full access to your computer. Call support yourself on a number you know.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of a fake update email.

subject.text: Your computer will be blocked within 24 hours

body.text: A critical update is missing on your computer. Open and install the attached file.
Turn off your antivirus while installing.

spots.label: Wrong domain
spots.explain: Your organisation uses idare.example. This is a different domain written with a hyphen.

spots.label: Urgency and threats
spots.explain: The threat of blocking is meant to make you act without thinking.

spots.label: Turn off antivirus
spots.explain: No real update asks you to switch off protection. This clears the way for malware.

spots.label: Executable file
spots.explain: An .exe file runs a program the moment you open it. Updates do not arrive this way.

scenes.prompt: Put the update steps in the right order.
scenes.explain: Saving protects your work, and the restart completes the update.

question.prompt: Your old phone no longer gets updates. What now?

options.label: Install antivirus and keep using it
options.feedback: Antivirus does not fix holes in the system itself.

options.label: Remove work accounts and move to a supported device
options.feedback: Correct. A device out of support will not get fixes for new holes.

options.label: Nothing, it still works fine
options.feedback: Working well does not mean safe. New holes will stay open.

scenes.explain: Keep no work accounts or data on a device out of support. Fully reset it before you sell it.

points: Install updates without delay, then restart.
Update only from Settings or the official store.
Keep no work data on unsupported devices.
